key_insight: Screening 50 solutes predicts that Ag, Ge, and Cd can enhance vacancy-mediated transport in bcc Li enough to reach 1 mA cm⁻² within their solubility limits.
engineering_relevance: Li–Ag at approximately 9 at.% Ag has a thermodynamically estimated critical current density of approximately 4 mA cm⁻² while retaining a theoretical capacity of 1522 mAh g⁻¹.
method: DFT screening using automated phase diagrams, solution energies, solute–vacancy binding energies, and experimental solubility limits.
Adapted dilute-limit Lomer model to estimate vacancy enhancement and critical current density.
Migration-barrier calculations and DFT-trained machine learning to assess trapping and accelerate solute filtering.
evidence_signal: Among 50 screened solutes, only Ag, Ge, and Cd were predicted to reach the 1 mA cm⁻² target within their solubility limits; Hume–Rothery rules alone were insufficient as prefilters.
watch_item: Vacancy trapping may partly offset the predicted enhancement, requiring further validation through molecular dynamics simulations.
paper_title: Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes for solid-state batteries: computational screening enabling high critical current density
